understood_action: Shortlist Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins first, but only if they reach the auction, and treat the score as a record of past pressure play, not a prediction.
confusions: Page is very long on a phone and the print is tiny; I could read headlines and the five-line box but not the fine detail. Lots of caveat tags (UNKNOWN, assumption, VERIFIED, pending) compete with the message. 'Clutch Score', '80% range', 'Persistence' and 'Plain plain ranking' are jargon; the box that says 'in plain words' still uses 'Runs Above Expected' and 'WPA'. Scores of 99 and 96 look like near-certain stars, yet the same page says they cannot be told apart, so I would not know whether to rank them. Pathirana is called 'Value Pick' while his score (98) is higher than Cummins's (96), which looks upside down. 'Plan A picks' versus 'RR group' record bars with Rs 21 cr walk-away cost are hard to square with a 15 cr budget.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: 'Must-Back' and 'Back' read like instructions that these players will deliver; 'Plan A' budget and a 'RR picks' comparison hint at a better next season. Page itself says it is not a forecast.

understood_action: Judge players on the balls that could swing the match (the high-pressure ones), and treat first-innings pressure labels with caution.
confusions: Mostly too small to read; I read the headings, the chart titles and the 'So what for RR' lines only. 'Pressure Index', 'leverage', 'WPA', 'win probability' and the heat-map axes (balls faced vs win probability?) mean nothing to me without a cricket-friendly gloss. Interactive chart with a slider and 'tap a point' is hard to use on a phone. Example balls table is eight near-identical cards with no clear point. Whether 'High' (80+) is rare or common is buried in text.
sounds_like_forecast: No; it is descriptive. Only the closing 'So what for RR' tells me to judge players this way, which is advice, not a forecast.

understood_action: Use the ranked list to build a long list of batters and bowlers who performed under pressure, not a strict order.
confusions: Longest, densest page; I could only read headlines and could not make out individual rows at this size. Headline says 'no two of the top 10 are clearly apart' so the ranking numbers (1, 2, 3...) contradict the message; I would still read 1 as best. Many rows carry 'UNKNOWN / assumption / likely retained' tags so I cannot tell who is actually buyable. Bar and range charts without a legend I can read. Rankings with bowlers and batters side by side invite comparing a Clutch Score of 99 for a batter with 99 for a bowler.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild; 'top 10', 'Likely retained' and 'Must-Back' may read as a prediction of who will be good or available. The page says historical only.

understood_action: Compare Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins and accept they are too close to call; choose on role and price, not on the score.
confusions: Readable at headline level only. 'Too close to call' is clear and useful. The radar chart with five axes (Skill, Consistency, Holds up, WPA per ball, High-pressure sample) is meaningless to me without a legend; I would not know which shape is 'better'. Table is a long stack of metric cards (RAE per 100, RSE, boundary %, wickets/dot %) with unexplained abbreviations, and dashes or 'UNKNOWN' fill most rows. Comparing a batter and a bowler is odd: the page says roles differ, so many rows are blank for one of them. Season-by-season line chart has few balls per season and is hard to read.
sounds_like_forecast: No explicit forecast; season chart could be misread as a trend heading into 2027.

understood_action: RR bats weakest under pressure in the middle and death overs, but the gap is not proven; protect bowling and do not spend on it.
confusions: Mostly too small to read beyond headlines. 'RR group today' versus 'The picks' own past record' versus 'League average' mixes three comparisons in similar-looking bars. The sign of the gap (minus = worse for batting, plus = better for bowling) is not obvious. Opening claim 'weakest area' conflicts with 'within noise, directional only'. 'Plan A picks have a strong record where RR is weak' is circular, because the picks were chosen for that record (the page admits this). 'Age UNKNOWN' and 'Overseas 7 of 20' look like facts but are inferred. Lineup and 20-over bowling plan sections look like a recommended XI, which I did not ask for.
sounds_like_forecast: Yes, moderately: 'Plan A' lineup, 'Best XI' and 'what this would change' imply a better 2027, even though it says 'past record, not a projection'.

understood_action: Chase the Must-Back and other shortlisted names only at or below the walk-away price, and use the swap rules if price goes too high.
confusions: Mostly too small to read; prices and the score-versus-price chart were unreadable at this size. Walk-away price is top of an assumed band, not a market price, which I could easily forget. Plan A total at walk-away (Rs 21 cr) exceeds the assumed 15 cr purse, and the real purse is reported as Rs 2.65 cr: I would not know which budget is true. 'Value Pick' and 'Hidden Gem' tiers are not sorted by score (Hidden Gem Ngidi 87 beats Value Pick Rizvi 80). 'Add to basket' buttons suggest a live buying tool.
sounds_like_forecast: Yes, somewhat: 'Must-Back', 'Value Pick', 'Hidden Gem' and 'Plan A/B' read as promised outcomes. Page says prices and availability are assumptions.

understood_action: Understand how the score is built and that it did not beat simple stats (strike rate or economy) at predicting next season, so use it only for shortlisting.
confusions: Readable at headline level. Honest and clear on the headline: 'did not beat a plain ranking'. But terms like Brier, shrinkage, persistence, 'interval', Pressure Index, 'Plain ranking' and weights (0.40, 0.25) mean nothing to me. Backtest bar chart (42.9 / 46.7 / 50.8) has three bars per group and the 'unassessable players left out vs counted as misses' split is confusing. I read 'batters 42.9 vs random pick 50.8' as the score being worse than random, which seems to say do not use it at all, yet the rest of the site relies on it.
sounds_like_forecast: No; this page is the strongest anti-forecast statement ('a record, not a forecast').

understood_action: Back Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins first; chase the other six only at or below the walk-away price.
confusions: Dense single page, but the top line is clear. The score and '80% range' columns are fine once explained, yet the table is ordered by tier, not score, so Pathirana (98.4) sits under Cummins (96.5) and Ngidi (87.3) under Rizvi (80.0), which looks like an error. Plan A at Rs 13.8 cr mid-price and Rs 21 cr walk-away against an assumed Rs 15 cr purse is confusing: the footer then says the real position (25-player squad, Rs 2.65 cr left) conflicts, so I cannot tell whether I can afford anyone. 'Do not chase' list gives 'Lowest scores in the assumed pool' next to 'popular but low score' with no price or reason I can act on. 'Gap fills' for bowlers says 'None measured' which could be misread as 'useless'. The 'Do the Plan A picks fix RR gaps?' box gives numbers (24.0 vs -9.7) with no explanation of per what.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: the heading title 'IPL 2027 auction' and 'Must-Back' imply promise. The honesty box at the top says clearly it is not a forecast.

understood_action: Back Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins first, if they reach the auction, and read the Clutch Score as a record, not a promise.
confusions: Very clear overall. Confusions: '110 players (47 batters and 71 bowlers)' does not add up until the all-rounders note is read. 'Clutch Reliability Score' versus 'Clutch Score' and '80% range' need the one-line explanation. Honest test line 'batters 42.9 v 46.7' is hard to read without knowing the first number is the score and the second a simple strike-rate list, and a selector may read 42.9 as a hit rate. Plan A 'Rs 13.8 cr at mid-price, Rs 21 cr at walk-away' against Rs 15 cr purse is confusing. Reported auction date '16 December 2026' is only in the footer.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: 'back these two first' reads as a recommendation that they will deliver; the title and item 5 disclaim it.

understood_action: Trust the score to be built fairly (fixed weights, small samples pulled toward average), but do not read it as a prediction.
confusions: Six steps are well put but 'Win chance', 'Pressure rating', 'Reliability (shrinkage)' and 'fair comparison' are still abstract. The weights table (Planned versus At work) is confusing: why does a planned 0.25 'match impact' become 0 for bowlers and 'skill' become 0.53? Footnote on 'Not Scorable (147 of 257)' is easy to skip but important. 'Skill under pressure: runs scored above ... versus an average player' is readable. The so-what line quotes weights, which is not an action.

understood_action: Judge players on the High-pressure balls (80+), where one over can move the match, and be careful with first-innings labels.
confusions: Bar chart of eight example balls is easy and good. Table of 'forecast error (Brier score)' by season and innings is the confusing bit: 0.25 'coin flip' and lower-is-better are hard to hold; the 2026 first-innings figure (0.240) is nearly a coin flip, which tells me pressure labels in the first innings are shaky, but it is not obvious. 'Medium' label overlaps the dashed line on the chart. '14-23% of balls each season' versus '80+ about the top 20%' feels inconsistent. Ranking 'earlier balls' language ('ranked against earlier balls') is hard to follow.

understood_action: Use the top-10 lists as a long list, not a strict order, because no two players are clearly apart.
confusions: Title says no two are clearly apart, yet the tables show ranks 1 to 10 with scores to one decimal, so I will read them as precise. Top batter (Vaibhav Sooryavanshi) and top bowler (Kuldeep Yadav) are RR squad or likely retained so are not targets; the page does not say who is actually buyable, only 'Pool UNKNOWN'. Bowlers' economy column header 'Econ*' and the asterisk explanation sit in small print. Batters Pathirana at 98.4 ranks third while Kuldeep 99.6 leads: nothing separates them. 'Likely retained' is defined only in the footnote.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: 'Likely retained' is a guess about next season; page tags it as an assumption.

understood_action: Chase eight names in three tiers: Sharma and Cummins first, hold everyone to the walk-away price.
confusions: Tier labels (Must-Back / Value Pick / Hidden Gem) are not in score order, so Hidden Gem Lungi Ngidi (87.3) beats Value Picks Rizvi, Samad, Iyer (about 80); the 'Why this tier' column explains it by lower end of range, but that is subtle. Pathirana 98.4 is Value Pick because he fills no measured gap: a selector might think that is a downgrade for a top-scoring bowler. 'Walk-away price = top of the price band' is in small type and price bands are assumptions. The mini bar chart at left is tiny, with error whiskers I cannot read.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: 'Must-Back', 'Value Pick' and 'Hidden Gem' sound like predictions of value; the so-what is framed as a task.

understood_action: Plan A picks look strong where RR bats are weak (middle and death overs), but this is past record, and the gaps are within noise.
confusions: The densest slide. Table 'Past record per 100 High-pressure balls' has negative and positive numbers with a dagger and balls in brackets, so I cannot tell which direction is good beyond 'higher is better'. 'Batting powerplay' shows -106.1 for the picks and +52.9 gap 'above league' for RR, which contradicts the title that RR's weakness is middle/death and is not explained. Gap table signs are hard to read (batting middle -7.3 is bad, bowling +1.8 is good). The title says 'strong record where RR is weak' while the footnote says the picks were chosen on that same record, which makes the claim circular. Budget notes 'Rs 21 cr at walk-away against Rs 15 cr purse' and 'real purse Rs 2.65 cr' undermine the plan. QR 'pending' box is noise.
sounds_like_forecast: Yes, mildly: the title mentions 'RR's 2027 performance' in the footnote and 'Plan A fixes gaps'; the slide repeatedly says 'not a projection'. Switch rules and Plan A/B sound like a firm plan.

understood_action: Use the score to build the shortlist and set walk-away prices, never as a forecast; for bowlers, check overall economy next to the score before bidding.
confusions: Clear title. Backtest bar chart (two panels, three colors each, 'left out' versus 'counted as misses') is hard to read: I took away that the Clutch Score top 10 beat 'random' only for bowlers and lost to the simple ranking in every case, which seems to say do not use it, and that makes slides 1 to 6 seem over-confident. 'Unassessable players' and 'persistence' are jargon. 'External facts: 0 verified of 29' is alarming without explanation. Long bullet list of limits is readable but long, and the bowler advice is buried in the so-what bar.
sounds_like_forecast: No; this slide explicitly states it is not a forecast.
